_finding: Robinhood stamps each quote with the time its server answered, so a quote held all weekend looked seconds old and the 'held' notes never fired. The recorder ages a bid/ask reference from when its mid last changed, kept across runs; and it writes the run row even when a run dies midway. And it prices a stock token only from pools against the chain's stables or wrapped ETH: on 09.11 memecoin pools paired with DJT priced it at ~$990.

mutations.name: the reference is re-dated on every run
mutations.find: if (!prev || prev.mid !== mid) state[address] = { mid, since: reference.quoted_at || atIso }
mutations.expect: FAIL an unchanged quote ages from when it was first seen

mutations.name: a run that throws writes no run row
the recorder does not pass the reference assets
mutations.find: const reading = pegReading(rec.address, rec.reference, pairs, { referenceAssets: C.referenceAssets })
mutations.expect: FAIL the recorder prices DJT from its USDG pool, not from the deeper memecoin pools

mutations.name: the wrapped native is left out of the reference assets
mutations.expect: FAIL Base: USDC and WETH, by address

mutations.name: a chain read that throws loses the reading
mutations.expect: FAIL a chain read that fails mid-run is named on the row, and the DexScreener reading stands

mutations.name: the chain breaker never opens
mutations.expect: FAIL after ONCHAIN_BREAKER failed tokens in a row the run stops asking the chain, and says so

mutations.name: the pool book stops learning once the breaker opens
mutations.expect: FAIL ...and the pool book still learned the pools DexScreener listed after the breaker

mutations.name: the chain is not merged when DexScreener is down
mutations.expect: FAIL with DexScreener down the chain alone gives the reading

mutations.name: an answer is copied for a reading with no premium
mutations.expect: FAIL a reading with no premium is not copied

mutations.name: an aggregator-only price carries a hash (the schema refuses the row)
mutations.expect: FAIL an unminted token is not read: two rows for three records
